newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK office space oversupply seen but outlook bright.
newsitem.headline: HK office space oversupply seen but outlook bright.

text.p: An oversupply of office space in Hong Kong over the next two years would put pressure on both capital values and rentals, but the long-term outlook of the office market remained positive, Hang Seng Bank said on Friday.
Despite an expected rebound in Hong Kong's economy, the take-up of offices may not be able to absorb increased supply, the bank said in its monthly economic report.
The overall vacancy rate may rise to 10.2 percent this year and 14.2 percent in 1998, from about 9.4 percent in 1995 and 8.2 percent last year, it said.
"This would inevitably put pressure on both office capital values and rentals," the report said.
But the longer term outlook was more positive as more multinationals and Chinese companies are expected to set up operations in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Bank report said.
"This would create more employment opportunities, increase demand for office space and further drive the development of Hong Kong as a service centre," it said.
The report said the office property market emerged from its two-year downturn in 1996, with prices rising 41.7 percent overall and 55.8 percent in the Central business district.
But rentals remained sluggish, declining five to six percent for quality offices, putting rental yields at their lowest levels ever, it said.

The price surge was attributable to the low 296,000 sq m in new supply in 1996, and the report noted new supply was expected to reach 567,000 sq m this year and 800,000 sq m in 1998 against the average of 459,000 during 1991 to 1995.
